tasks.short: Interpret diagnostic test results to make appropriate differential diagnoses.

steps.what: Read the referral that names which diagnostic tests to interpret
Examine the patient while the diagnostic results are interpreted
Read stored diagnostic test results on the allergy record
Draft a numeric summary of stored diagnostic test results
Name appropriate differential diagnoses from the patient and the summary
Check the differential diagnoses interpret the diagnostic results
Commit the accepted differential diagnosis on the allergy record

tasks.design: The {OTHER} allergy record already holds each diagnostic result and the reference interval printed on it. A draft only lines those numbers up. The allergist still names the appropriate differential diagnoses after the examination. A later check accepts that wording, and only then is that version committed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The numbers and the diagnosis sat in one dictated note, so a rule could not write the differential without also deciding it.
tasks.enabler_now: The result and its reference interval can be copied as fields. Naming the differential stays a separate human step.
tasks.still_hard: Many results still arrive as scanned pages. A missing interval means no summary is drafted.
tasks.human_edge: Only the allergist can say which diagnosis fits this patient. The numeric summary does not do that.
tasks.altitude: The same examinations stay. Less time goes to retyping test numbers. The allergist gains no new right to diagnose.

reach.task: Interpret allergy test results in primary care
reach.learn: Which stored fields a summary may line up, and which differential the physician must still name.

evidence.claim: A stored result can be lined up with the reference interval printed on that same result. That lineup does not name a diagnosis.
Medical-device software sits in AI Act Annex I, and AI that needs a notified body is high-risk. The numeric draft does not decide a diagnosis.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a legal basis. The allergist accepts the diagnosis before it is committed.

assumptions: Means were rounded by largest remainder. The small spreadsheet prior is folded into screens because the test values live on the allergy record.
The allergist writes the summary and the diagnosis today, so every step's actor is the allergist. The machine is only the future fate of the summary and of the commit.

The stored diagnostic results step is the producer. Fields are the analyte, the value, the unit, and the reference interval already on the result. If a result is free text, the allergist types the summary while naming the diagnosis.
The summary is an ungated draft. It is not the accepted diagnosis. The check names accepted differential diagnosis v1 and does not rewrite it. The commit writes that version and does not edit it.
No focal incremental hours. Exceptions stay inside the check. System upkeep is the field map only.
unknowns: Whether this record stores wheal size, specific IgE, and spirometry as fields or only as scanned pages.
research_questions: Which diagnostic results are discrete fields today, and which still arrive as images?

already_counted.description: Reading the differential against the patient and the results, inside the check.

incremental.description: Map result value, unit, and reference interval for the numeric summary.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the result has no stored value or reference interval, so no summary is drafted. High is 8 when the summary and the commit run and naming the differential stays in full. Central net is the summary plus the commit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Document patients' medical histories spoken in the room
Read earlier mail about this patient's medical history
Read the medical history already stored for this patient
Enter the new medical history on the allergy record
Draft history sentences that each cite an entered field

loop.input: Entered history fields and the stored medical history.
loop.output: History sentences, each naming one entered field or one stored field.
loop.check: A sentence that names neither an entered field nor a stored field is dropped.
loop.stop: One pass. If no sentence remains, the draft is empty.
loop.why_not_simpler: A blank history form cannot write this patient's sentences from the fields just entered.

steps.what: Check the medical history against what the patient said
Commit the accepted medical history on the allergy record

tasks.design: The allergist still takes the history in the room and enters the fields on {OTHER}. A bounded draft writes sentences that each cite an entered field or a stored field, using any earlier {EMAIL} only as context the allergist already read. The allergist checks the sentences against what the patient said. The accepted medical history is committed in a later step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The history was one free-text note. A form could not turn that note into sentences that stay tied to what was said.
tasks.enabler_now: The allergist already enters allergen, onset, and drug fields. A draft can be limited to those fields, and the clinician still validates before write-back.
tasks.still_hard: If the history is only free text, the draft is empty and the allergist writes it during the check.
tasks.human_edge: The allergist hears what the patient meant. A sentence that cites a field can still be the wrong history.
tasks.altitude: The same time stays with the patient. Less time goes to writing the history narrative. The allergist still decides what enters the dossier.

reach.learn: Which fields the nurse enters so each history sentence can cite one, and that the nurse still checks the wording.

evidence.claim: The clinician validates a drafted consultation note before it is written into the record.
History sentences can be limited to fields the allergist just entered and fields already stored. A sentence with neither source can be dropped.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a legal basis. The allergist accepts the history before it is committed.
Providers remain responsible for careful use of generative tools, including medication errors from wrong registration.
Recording how staff work needs works-council consent.

assumptions: Means were rounded by largest remainder. The small spreadsheet prior is folded into screens because history fields live on the allergy record.
The allergist writes the history today, so the actor on the draft and on the commit is the allergist. The machine is only the future fate of that writing.

Entered fields are allergen, onset, reaction, and current drug. The stored-history step is the producer of older fields. The room is not recorded, so works-council consent for staff monitoring is not part of this design.
The narrative is an ungated draft. The loop check only drops a sentence with no field. The person check names accepted medical history v1. The commit does not edit that version.
No focal incremental hours. Exceptions stay inside the check. Allergy histories are health data, so access control is in the build.
unknowns: Whether this clinic enters history as fields or as one free-text note.
National rules if a later design adds room recording.
research_questions: Which history items are fields today, and which are typed only in the narrative?

already_counted.description: Reading history sentences against what the patient said, inside the check.

incremental.description: Map allergen, onset, reaction, and drug fields the history sentences may cite.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the history was not entered as fields, so the draft is empty and the allergist writes it in the check. High is 16 when most sentences cite a field and the visit and the check stay in full. Central net is the draft plus the commit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop individualized treatment plans for patients from preferences, clinical data, and therapy risks.

steps.what: Hear patients state preferences during the treatment visit
Read mail on patient preferences and earlier therapies
Read stored clinical data on therapies for this patient
Read risks and benefits of therapies in the protocol
Draft therapy options with the stated risks and benefits
Develop the individualized treatment plan considering patient preferences
Check individualized treatment plans against preferences and clinical data
Commit the accepted treatment plan on the allergy record

tasks.design: The allergist hears preferences in the room, reads earlier {EMAIL}, and reads stored clinical data on {OTHER}. The therapy protocol in {DOCS} is the source of stated risks and benefits. A draft lists matching options and does not choose. The allergist develops the individualized treatment plan, a later check accepts it, and a separate step commits that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Options, preferences, and the chosen plan were one letter, so copying the protocol also looked like the decision.
tasks.enabler_now: A protocol can list options with their risks and benefits. The choice stays in the visit.
tasks.still_hard: Preferences are often spoken once and never stored. A protocol that is not a controlled document cannot feed the draft.
tasks.human_edge: The plan has to fit what this patient will actually do. The options list does not know that.
tasks.altitude: The same conversation about preferences stays. Less time goes to copying protocol options. The draft does not give a right to prescribe.

reach.task: Develop an allergy treatment plan with the patient
reach.learn: Preferences stay in the visit. The protocol draft is a list of options, not the plan.

evidence.claim: A protocol can list therapy options with the risks and benefits it already states. Selecting the plan is a separate step.
The medicines act defines what a prescription is. Writing this plan does not create that document.
Providers remain responsible for careful use of generative tools, including medication errors from wrong registration.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs a legal basis. The allergist accepts the plan before it is committed.

assumptions: The published means sum to 100.1. Shares were floored and the two leftover points went to the largest fractions, meetings then mail. The spreadsheet prior is folded into screens because clinical data live on the allergy record.
The allergist writes the plan today, so the actor on the options draft and on the commit is the allergist. The machine is only the future fate of copying options and of committing the accepted plan.

Stored clinical data fields are allergen, severity, and current therapy. The protocol fields are therapy name, stated risk, and stated benefit. The person who reads the protocol is the producer of that text.
The options draft is ungated and is not a choice. The check names accepted treatment plan v1. The commit does not edit it. This task does not send a prescription.
No focal incremental hours. Exceptions stay inside the check.
unknowns: Whether a controlled therapy protocol exists in the document system, with risks and benefits as readable text.
research_questions: Does the local protocol list risks and benefits per therapy in text a draft can quote without rewording?

already_counted.description: Reading the plan against preferences and clinical data, inside the check.

incremental.description: Map protocol option, risk, and benefit text onto allergen and current-therapy fields.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the protocol is not a readable document, so no options draft runs. High is 8 when the options draft and the commit run and the plan is still written in the visit. Central net is the options draft plus the commit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess the risks and benefits of therapies for allergic and immunologic disorders.

steps.what: Discuss the therapies with the patient in the room
Read the note about these allergic and immunologic therapies
Read stored dose and contraindication for these therapies
Draft stored dose and contraindication facts for these therapies
Assess risks and benefits of therapies for allergic and immunologic disorders
Check the risk assessment against the patient and the facts
Commit the accepted risk benefit assessment on the record

tasks.design: The assessment stays with the allergist in the room. {OTHER} only copies the dose and contraindication already stored for these therapies, after the allergist has read them and any {EMAIL} note. The allergist assesses risks and benefits for the allergic and immunologic disorders. A later check accepts that assessment, and a separate step commits it without changing the wording.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dose, contraindication, and the benefit judgement were written as one paragraph, so copying a fact looked like the assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: A drug reference already holds dose and contraindication. Copying those fields does not judge benefit.
tasks.still_hard: Benefit depends on this patient's goals. Stored contraindications miss what was never coded.
tasks.human_edge: The allergist weighs benefit for this disorder. A copied contraindication is not that judgement.
tasks.altitude: The assessment is unchanged and stays at the same length. Only the copy of stored dose and contraindication leaves the allergist's hands. No right to prescribe moves.

reach.task: Assess allergy therapy risks before dispensing
reach.learn: Dose and contraindication are stored facts. The benefit judgement stays with the prescriber.

evidence.claim: A drug reference checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates.
Copying a stored dose and contraindication into a fact list does not assess benefit.
The medicines act defines what a prescription is. This assessment does not create that document.
Providers remain responsible for careful use of generative tools, including medication errors from wrong registration.

assumptions: Means were rounded by largest remainder. The spreadsheet prior is folded into screens because dose and contraindication live on the allergy record.

The allergist writes the assessment today, so the actor on the fact draft and on the commit is the allergist. The machine is only the future fate of copying those facts and of committing the accepted assessment.
The read of stored dose and contraindication is the producer. The draft copies those two fields and does not add an interaction judgement. If they are free text, no fact draft runs.
The fact list is an ungated draft. The assessment stays at full remaining time. The check names accepted risk benefit assessment v1. The commit does not edit it.
No focal incremental hours. Exceptions stay inside the check. This task does not prescribe.
unknowns: Whether dose and contraindication are stored as fields or only inside free text.
research_questions: Which therapies have a coded dose and contraindication on this record today?

already_counted.description: Reading the assessment against the patient and the copied facts, inside the check.

incremental.description: Map dose and contraindication fields for the fact list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when dose and contraindication are only free text, so no fact list is drafted. High is 4 when the fact list and the commit run and the assessment stays in full. Central net is the fact list plus the commit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The same time stays with the patient and with naming the differential, the plan, and the risk. Less time goes to retyping test numbers, history sentences, and stored doses. No new right to diagnose or to prescribe.
skills_to_grow: Enter history fields and confirm stored test values before a draft runs.
Refuse a differential, a plan, or a risk note when the stored fields do not match the patient in the room.
role.ambitious_version: The allergist could open the visit with test numbers and protocol options already beside the record, and still name the differential in the room.
